Star orbiting close to Sagittarius A* could reveal its spin — plus, how exoskeletons might change the way humans move.

item.title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10951-4

Functional lymphoid structures within the skull bone marrow enable central nervous system immunosurveillance and shape immune responses to brain disease.

item.title: Observation of conformal field theory spectra in a quantum simulator
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10904-x

Measurements on an array of optically trapped neutral atoms at a quantum phase transition provide a direct observation of the universal excitation spectrum predicted by conformal field theory.

item.title: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10928-3

Whole-brain activity mapping, targeted cell manipulations and electrophysiology in mice identify wake-activated neuronal populations that are crucial for sleep drive and can persistently reduce daily sleep amount.

item.title: Increasing CO<sub>2</sub> levels fertilize C<sub>4</sub> grass production
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10935-4

By combining a meta-analysis of CO2 enrichment experiments with three decades of southern African savanna observations, an increase in biomass production by C4 grasses under rising CO2 levels in water-limited environments is revealed.

item.title: A global atmospheric methane record from a tropical ice core
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10938-1

A 2,000-year Peruvian ice core record of atmospheric CH4 concentrations contains the first historical global CH4 record from the low latitudes, and implementation of a four-box model indicates higher equatorial CH4 strength than previous estimates from polar-only records.

item.title: Family genetic designs in MoBa provide insights into health and functioning
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10926-5

The Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study demonstrates how family-based genomic data can disentangle direct genetic effects from confounding, improving studies of health and human development.

item.title: Asymmetric prefrontal representations for leader–follower dynamics
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10900-1

Mice spontaneously form leader and follower roles during cooperation, and the medial prefrontal cortex encodes these role dynamics and an egocentric social value map of the partner’s position.

item.title: Atomic-scale double-slit interferometry with a focused electron probe
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10914-9

Double-slit interferometry at the atomic scale is demonstrated using scanning transmission electron microscopy to provide evidence of interference fringes generated with a focused electron beam encountering two silicon atomic columns separated by 1.36 Å.

item.title: Synthesis of pyrroles from isoxazoles by an O-to-C skeletal edit
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10933-6

A one-pot skeletal-editing reaction replaces isoxazole oxygen with carbon to form challenging pyrroles, enabled by an N-propargylic enaminone intermediate and a computational model predicting reaction outcomes.

item.title: Human brain organoids record the passage of time over multiple years
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10877-x

Human brain organoids were developed for over five years in culture to demonstrate that brain cells can continue to mature and record the passage of time, following human-specific endogenous programs, even outside the context of the organism.

item.title: Multiyear tropical warm pool warming drives slowdown in Antarctic mass loss
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10912-x

Recent Antarctic ice mass gain was linked to a recurrent atmospheric teleconnection, but this recurs about once per decade in observations and historical simulations so does not yet reflect a global-warming-driven moistening of Antarctica.

item.title: The HydroGym reinforcement learning platform for fluid dynamics
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10917-6

HydroGym offers over 60 standardized reinforcement-learning flow-control environments and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to a 3D wing, cutting local skin friction by 38% and exploration costs by four orders of magnitude.

item.title: An Icelandic pangenome reference
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10924-7

Newly developed methods enable construction of Icelandic haplotypes and mapping of population-scale short reads to a pangenome by reducing reference bias and improving discovery in low-mappability regions, revealing many novel variants, including pathogenic alleles.

item.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10910-z

The psychedelic psilocybin reorganizes brain activity into structured, context-aligned patterns that integrate internal and external processing, providing a neural basis for the felt continuity between self and world, elucidating how the psychedelic state translates into psychological change.

item.title: Discovery of a star sensitive to the spin of Sagittarius A*
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10894-w

The discovery of the fast-orbiting star S301 near Sagittarius A* offers a promising new probe of the central black hole spin of the Milky Way through relativistic orbit measurements.

item.title: Safety and security of large language models in healthcare
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10687-1

The Review examines rapid LLM adoption in clinical care, outlining emerging security and safety risks across development stages, key protective layers, clinically relevant threats and current mitigation responsibilities in a single integrated framework.

item.title: Pervasive phosphorylation by phage T7 kinase disarms bacterial defences
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10934-5

The T7 bacteriophage deactivates bacterial defence systems through T7K phosphorylation of nearly all host and phage proteins during infection.

item.title: A biased allosteric modulator is a molecular glue for β<sub>2</sub>AR dimerization
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10892-y

AP-7-168, an optimized derivative of a β-arrestin-biased negative allosteric modulator of the β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR), functions as a molecular glue to stabilize β2AR homodimerization.

item.title: Virus deploys a ‘loose cannon’ enzyme to overpower bacterial defences
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02537-x

Viruses that infect bacteria must either evade or counter the defence systems of their host. The viral kinase enzyme T7K has been found to phosphorylate nearly all bacterial proteins, but its specificity for DNA-binding proteins enables it to disable defence systems that target nucleic acids.

item.title: How do people live beyond 110? Abundance of cancer-killing cells might be key
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02587-1

Research on people 110 years and older reveals an immune system that continues to adapt.

item.title: Psychedelics tune the brain to the environment
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02377-9

Rather than just scrambling neural activity, the psychedelic substance psilocybin also reorganizes brain dynamics so as to align with a person’s context and experiences.

item.title: Computational ‘gym’ trains AI models to control turbulence
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02375-x

The HydroGym computational environment teaches agents strategies for fluid-flow control that can be applied to scenarios they have not encountered before.

item.title: Human organoids that mimic brain development grown for years in lab
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02585-3

Models of how the brain changes over time could help researchers to understand how diseases affect the organ later in life.

item.title: Activity of solar-driven polymer catalysts unleashed to produce a potential green fuel
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02373-z

Engineering of polymer crystals has vastly increased the activity of these materials as catalysts for producing hydrogen fuel from water, using only sunlight.

item.title: The Antarctic ice sheet has gained mass — but probably not for long
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02376-w

Since 2020, snowfall has largely counterbalanced the melting of the Antarctic ice sheet. The atmospheric effect that causes this has been identified — and it’s temporary.

item.title: Too much mate choice overwhelms frogs
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02554-w

Female treefrogs select less carefully when hearing a chorus of males.
